relevance_note: Mother and daughter carry a TNFAIP3 variant: 'This revealed a heterozygous NM_001270508.2: c.608T > G, p.(Leu203Arg) missense variant of TNFAIP3 in both patients'.
method_note: Read the paper in full and built the JSON with a Python script in my scratch directory; every value was typed from my reading, and the script only resolved typed spans to the paper's exact characters (the paper uses no-break and four-per-em spaces, e.g. in 'c.608T > G' and 'IgA < 0.06') and then checked each span verbatim. Table 1 has patients as rows (P1 = Patient 1, mother; P2 = Patient 2, daughter); the P1 row contains a line break inside the Igs cell, so P1 full-row spans include that newline. Labels: Patient 1 is also 'P1' and 'D001', Patient 2 also 'P2' and 'D002' in figures. Individuals: besides the two patients I recorded 'Brother of P1' (pedigree legend: died at 40, history of rheumatism and thyroid disease; not genotyped) and 'L001', a CVID patient used as a control who carries TNFAIP3 c.1309del (p.Ala437Profs); the authors' patient count (2) excludes L001. No one is called proband; is_proband is null for the patients (WES was run on the mother, segregation by Sanger in the daughter). Inheritance for the daughter left 'not reported' because the paper does not state the variant's parental origin in words (rule 8), though both mother and daughter carry it. TNFRSF13B c.310T > C (p.Cys104Arg) is attributed to the mother only; the Discussion states its 'absence in the daughter'. Ages 49 (P1) and 29 (P2) are ages at first presentation to the authors' centre; recorded as onset of the presenting features, not as age at diagnosis or last evaluation, which the paper does not give. Inconsistencies/tensions: (1) Table 1 gives P1 age at onset '18 years' but the text reports 'a childhood history of oral and genital ulcers'; (2) Table 1 gives P2 onset '9 years' while the text says ulcers 'since adolescence'; (3) treatments differ between text and Table 1 (P1 table adds methotrexate and IgRT; P2 table adds anakinra and golimumab; text adds methylprednisolone, dexamethasone, azithromycin), all recorded; (4) the iliac occlusion was 'without features typical of vasculitis' on CT, but skin biopsy showed leucocytoclastic vasculitis; treated as different sites, vasculitis checklist 'observed'; (5) pathogenicity is 'likely pathogenic variant effect' (MetaRNN) in Results but 'novel pathogenic variant' in the Conclusion; both quoted. Checklist judgement calls: P1 GI inflammation 'observed' from a single 'bout of gastroenteritis' (possibly infectious); P1 cytopenia (autoimmune) left 'not reported' because leukopenia and pernicious anemia are not called autoimmune cytopenias; P2 type 1 diabetes 'excluded' from 'no signs of insulin deficiency'; P2 diarrhea not mapped to GI inflammation; brother's 'rheumatism' and 'thyroid disease' not mapped to arthritis or autoimmune thyroiditis. No group statements were used.

Despite undergoing a percutaneous transluminal angioplasty, she ultimately required a lower leg amputation.

functional_evidence_statement.value: Reduced A20 expression in patient PBMCs (A20/actin ratio after TNFα: P1 0.205 vs mean HC 0.802); HEK293T overexpression of the mutant: reduced A20 (A20/actin 0.28 vs 1.18 wild-type) with increased TRAF6 and phosphorylated IκBα; patient PBMCs showed increased phosphorylation in NF-κB, STAT1 and mTOR pathways and elevated pro-inflammatory cytokine production; pro-inflammatory serum cytokine profile in both patients
span: showed a significantly lower A20/actin ratio in patients compared to HCs, particularly after stimulation with TNFα (P1: 0.205; P2 0.218; L001 0.453 versus mean ratio HC:0.802
In this model, mutant A20 expression was consistently reduced, while levels of TRAF6 and, to a lesser extent, phosphorylated IκBα were increased following TNFα stimulation
After stimulation, the A20/actin ratio was 1.18 for wild-type and 0.28 for mutant.
Patient-derived PBMCs demonstrated reduced A20 expression, increased phosphorylation within the NF-κB, STAT1, and mTOR pathways, and elevated production of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
Measurement of circulating serum cytokines demonstrated a clear pro-inflammatory profile in both patients as compared to the HCs
